selfReview.type: AI own-locale direct Japanese semantic and continuous Khmer prose self-review
selfReview.method: Translated every distinct Japanese paragraph once in an exact source-keyed Khmer map and checked each contextual use before expansion. Compared complete explanations, dialogues, question stems/options and all four source-specific rationales directly with Japanese, reviewing connected Khmer prose and preserving full actors, conditions, uncertainty and sequence. Source bindings were revalidated after the final wording adjustment.
semanticChecks: ADL/IADL remain distinct and activity-specific; ability in one activity does not prove another. Movement includes the person’s life purpose and wishes, not only location change. Posture names do not establish stability or a universal bed angle.

Pressure, friction/shear, limb trapping, pain, breathing, skin and support conditions remain explicit. Bed height for worker burden differs from height for foot support at edge-sitting. All clinical methods remain conditional on individual state/plan, equipment instructions and trained technique.

Wheelchair components retain separate functions: parking vs attendant brake, caster/drive-wheel/handrim, leg vs foot support and tipping lever. Footplate is not a boarding step; tire pressure may affect parking brake. Faulty equipment is not compensated by grip strength.

Route checking and person explanation/destination notification stay assigned to Tanaka and Kishimoto respectively. Unknown route is not called safe merely because checking was requested. Route changes are explained before movement.

Turning, rising to sit and standing remain separate actions with separate current-state checks. Hemiplegic examples protect affected shoulder/arm; no pulling a paralyzed arm, neck hanging, dragging skin or forced knee pressure. Example orientation/staffing is not universalized to all people/times.

Dizziness, new pain, knee buckling and unsupported feet retain pause/safe-support/report conditions and explicit responsible or medical-professional recipients. Completion of one movement is not proof of stable sitting/standing or ability to release support for clothing tasks.

Disuse syndrome is not diagnosed from a short rest request. Pressure-injury prevention combines skin/site observation, activity, pressure relief, support surface and nutrition in an individual plan. No self-diagnosis, drug selection or rubbing redness; normal sacrum does not negate red heel.

Cane gait three actions vs two preserve exact cane/affected/unaffected sequence and stability comparison. Stairs preserve different ascent/descent sequences, prior cane placement and helper on the lower-step side. Knowledge of sequence alone does not authorize clinical technique.

Visual-impairment guidance preserves identity/location announcement, consent, preferred contact, personal pace, advance path-change information and explicit right/left reference. No sudden wrist pulling, pushing or unannounced handoff.

Transfer prep, transfer completion, post-transfer stability and wheelchair departure remain separate. Curb/reverse-descent examples retain equipment/surface/training limits; reverse travel does not make an uncontrollable slope safe. No testing arm strength after entering an unsafe slope.

Voluntary participation: not now differs from all-day absence; the stated younger-sister call is retained only where source specifies it.14:05is notification time,14:30is late-entry deadline, call-end and participation choice remain unknown; Kishimoto rechecks after the call.

Updated14:20start differs from old14:00notice and does not determine consent/participation or mobility method. Notice correction is planned, not completed.13:20minus15minutes is13:05assembly, not an actual departure record.

All66questions have four individually translated source-specific rationales. The24explicit-empty readings remain empty strings and42effective nonempty readings are translated without replacing them with summaries.
